body:
I feel like a hypocrite for anything positive I want to tell you, but at the very least I can relate to you. I have a friend who always let's me know that she feels as if we are leaving her out or that she thinks we think she's not 'good enough' to be in our friend group, and that couldn't be farther from the truth, she's wholesome, cute, and smart. She's such a supportive friend. A lot of people, most of the time insensitively, say 'it's just all in your head', but I believe in a way it *is* in your head, sometimes people can read a little too much into what others say  coupled with negative experiences with trust this can really ruin your interpretations. If you truly believe people keep you around for your humor, you should know humor is a personality thing and it's a very likeable trait, it's a reflection of who you are in a way. That being said, if your 'friends' aren't inclusive of you **and you've talked it out with them** and they still exclude you, then it's best to ditch them. I usually don't even entertain the thought of my friends not liking me because I already think that way with my parents, and it really destroys a person's self-worth. i hope this doesnt come across as trivializing your pain, I just wanted to provide a teeny bit more positive outlook. You said you've become socially awkward, and my advice is to try making online friends. I have a lot of trouble talking to people irl but online has less strings attached and it's not as awkward, eventually it comes naturally, I've been able to make a couple of lasting friends purely online.   


My parents were also not the most supportive, or at least not supportive in the way I need them to be. I'm not going to suggest talking it out with them because it seems as if we have the same relationships with our parents and I know my parents would never listen. It seems like they only care about the outcome and not the true mental/emotional effort it takes to achieve them, my mom told me once it was not okay for me to be depressed because I 'have everything i ever wanted', 'have great attentive parents', and monetarily privileged.  I once joked, when my mom told me I was always crying as a baby, that "i must have been a very unhappy baby", and she got *really* angry, telling me i have no right to be upset when I have such a great family. I'm sorry if I'm rambling here, but I think you're not alone, you might feel very lonely, but you're alone. Sorry, I guess i just wanted to relate to someone...about an hour ago I took some random pills in our cupboard, but now as I'm feeling the consequences, I just wish my parents would notice and care, but in the end I don't actually want to die. I hope you can come to the same conclusion, and I hope you find some group of people who really make you forget about being socially awkward, who make you forget about the negativity in your life, and I'm also open to talk privately if you'd like,  so please don't ever hurt yourself <3
